pathways(): the bridge between the three families

honets

2026-08-26

The analytic question

The three structure families in honets are entry points into one another, not islands. pathways() is the generic that carries a fitted memory network across to the other two: it extracts the paths the model considers real and returns them as plain strings, which build_simplicial(type = "pathway") turns into a complex.

It is a small verb doing one job, and it is the reason a HON can be handed to a topological analysis without any manual reshaping.

library(honets)
seqs <- split(human_long$code, human_long$session_id)
library(cograph)

Three methods, one generic

pathways() dispatches on net_hon, net_hypa and net_mogen. Each returns the paths that model regards as meaningful — which is a different set in each case, because the three models mean different things by “meaningful”.

hon <- build_hon(seqs, max_order = 2, min_freq = 50)
p_hon <- pathways(hon)
length(p_hon)
[1] 25
pathways(hon, top = 6)
[1] "Specify Command -> Specify"   "Command Request -> Specify"  
[3] "Specify Command -> Request"   "Request Specify -> Interrupt"
[5] "Command Command -> Command"   "Command Specify -> Interrupt"

From a HON: the extracted rules — contexts that earned their own node. 25 of them at min_freq = 50.

hp <- build_hypa(seqs, order = 2)
p_hypa <- pathways(hp)
length(p_hypa)

From HYPA: the anomalous paths — those significantly over- or under-represented against the degree-preserving null. 185 of them. Note the first entry, Interrupt Interrupt -> Interrupt: the same repeated- interruption pattern that path_dependence() flags as the highest-divergence context.

mo <- build_mogen(seqs, max_order = 2)
p_mogen <- pathways(mo)
length(p_mogen)
[1] 702
pathways(mo, top = 4)
[1] "Specify Command -> Specify"   "Command Request -> Specify"  
[3] "Specify Command -> Request"   "Request Specify -> Interrupt"

From MOGen: every path in the fitted layer — 702, the complete second-order transition set, because a multi-order model does not prune.

The format

Each string is "<context states, space separated> -> <next state>". The context uses spaces so that the arrow separates history from continuation unambiguously.

p_hon[1]
[1] "Specify Command -> Specify"

Read as: the context Specify Command continuing to Specify.

Crossing to the simplicial family

sc <- build_simplicial(hon, type = "pathway")
sc
Pathway Complex 
  9 nodes, 29 simplices, dimension 2
  Density: 22.5%  |  Mean dim: 0.90  |  Euler: 1
  f-vector: (f0=9 f1=14 f2=6)
  Betti: b0=2 b1=1
  Nodes: Command, Correct, Frustrate, Inquire, Interrupt, Refine, Request, Specify, Verify

build_simplicial() calls pathways() internally — you rarely need to call it yourself. Each path becomes a simplex, and because a simplicial complex is closed under subsets, so does every sub-path. The result has a geometry, and therefore a topology: b0 = 2 says the well-evidenced pathways fall into two disconnected groups of actions, and b1 = 1 says there is one one-dimensional hole — a cycle of actions that is never closed by an observed pathway.

Neither statement is available from the transition network the paths came from.

Seeing them

Whichever model produced them, pathways draw the same way — as blobs over the first-order nine-node layout. The higher-order object supplies the pathways; it is never the thing drawn. Compare the sources by eye: HON gives the contexts that earned a node, HYPA the ones that deviate from the null, MOGen every fitted path.

net1 <- build_hon(seqs, max_order = 1)
plot_simplicial(net1,
                pathways = as.data.frame(hon, order_min = 2,
                                         sort_by = "count", top = 6),
                max_pathways = 6, title = "Pathways from build_hon()")

plot_simplicial(hp, anomaly = "over", max_pathways = 6,
                dismantled = TRUE, ncol = 3)

The choice of source model matters

Because the three models select different paths, they build different complexes:

do.call(rbind, lapply(
  list(HON = hon, HYPA = hp, MOGen = mo),
  function(m) {
    s <- build_simplicial(m, type = "pathway")
    data.frame(paths = length(pathways(m)), simplices = s$n_simplices,
               dimension = s$dimension, b0 = betti_numbers(s)[1])
  }))
      paths simplices dimension b0
HON      25        29         2  2
HYPA    185       105         2  1
MOGen   702       129         2  1

MOGen’s 702 unpruned paths produce a dense, connected complex; HON’s 25 well-evidenced rules produce a sparse, disconnected one. The topology you report is a property of the model you chose, not of the raw sequences — say which model, and say why.

Calling it directly

You would call pathways() yourself to inspect what a model considers real, or to feed the paths somewhere else:

# how long are the extracted paths?
table(lengths(strsplit(p_hon, " ", fixed = TRUE)))

 4 
25

What to do next

  • build_simplicial() — the main consumer, and where the topology gets computed.
  • build_hon(), build_hypa(), build_mogen() — the three producers.
  • window_hypergraph() — the other route out of sequence data, into the hypergraph family.
